title: Equal scalar defects split the tensor product with an opposite algebra
statement: Let $K$ be a field, $S$ its separable closure, and $A,B$ finite-dimensional central simple $K$-algebras. Let $x,y$ belong to the second continuous Galois cohomology of $S^\times$ [def-sc-galois-units-cohomology], with its natural Galois action and discrete coefficient topology. Suppose $R(A,x)$ and $R(B,y)$ are scalar-defect realizations [def-sc-brauer-scalar-defect] and $x=y$. Then there exists an integer $n>0$ and a $K$-algebra isomorphism $A\otimes_K B^{\mathrm{op}}\cong M_n(K)$.

proof.text: Choose the splitting matrices and locally constant lifts in the two realizations. Transposition gives a splitting of the opposite of B; its lifts are inverse transposes. Kronecker tensoring gives a splitting of A⊗Bop whose scalar defect is the quotient c_z/c_w of the two scalar defects.

Equality of the homogeneous degree-two cohomology classes implies z−w is a continuous homogeneous boundary. Evaluating its witnessing one-cochain at (1,g) gives a locally constant scalar cochain a with c_z(g,h)/c_w(g,h)=a(g)g(a(h))/a(gh). Rescaling the tensor lifts by a(g) inverse makes their scalar defect trivial, so they form a genuine GL cocycle.

The rescaled cocycle is locally constant on the compact Galois group. Choose an open normal subgroup on whose cosets the cocycle is constant and which fixes its finitely many matrix entries and the finitely many splitting coefficients. The cocycle is one on this subgroup and factors through the finite Galois quotient with coefficients in its fixed field. Finite Galois descent of vector spaces trivializes this matrix cocycle. Conjugate the splitting by the trivializing matrix so that its descent action is entrywise Galois action. Fixed points then give A⊗Bop ≅ M_n(K), where n is the product of the positive original splitting sizes. This proves tensor splitting without invoking Brauer equivalence.
